bullets.title: FOMC Setup: Easing Bias Removal Expected; Gamma/SOXL Flows Support Pre-Decision Melt-Up
bullets.body: SpotGamma estimates $5B+ in positive gamma supporting SPX into Wednesday's FOMC; consensus expects the Fed to remove its easing bias from the statement, though any hawkish commentary may be offset by Warsh signals on cuts. Separately, SOXL required $9B+ in rebalancing buys yesterday — roughly one-third of typical monthly 401k equity flows — which has been a mechanical driver of semiconductor price action rather than fundamentals. Post-OPEX, correlation (COR1M at 8) is near levels that historically preceded volatility spikes.

bullets.title: May Housing Starts -15.4% M/M on Multifamily Collapse; Negligible GDP Impact
bullets.body: May housing starts fell sharply to 1,177k vs. 1,430k consensus, driven by a >40% drop in multi-unit starts while single-family declined only ~2%. Analysts view the pullback as mean-reversion from starts running above permit levels rather than a new downtrend; 2Q residential investment contribution is now tracked at ~0.5% q/q SAAR. A modest 3Q rebound is expected as lower prices and improving employment support demand.

bullets.title: Core PCE Tracking 3.44% Y/Y in May; Inflation Still Running Hot
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley holds its May core PCE forecast at 0.36% m/m (headline 0.48%), which would push the y/y rate to 3.44% from 3.31% in April. The 6-month annualized pace accelerated to 4.20% from 3.83%, with airfares re-accelerating +7% m/m in import prices. PCE data releases June 25.

bullets.title: ADP Weekly Hiring Slows to +25.5K 4-Week Avg; AI Uncertainty Weighing on Labor
bullets.body: The ADP 4-week average for private employment fell to +25.5k (week ending 5/30) from +29.0k the prior week, covering ~26M private workers. Hiring described as muted with AI-related uncertainty persisting as a headwind; the data excludes federal workers.

bullets.title: Mag7 Leadership Deteriorating; Market Broadening Toward Small Caps, Materials, Cyclicals
bullets.body: 22V notes Mag7/hyperscaler performance has been deteriorating while small caps significantly outperform — Russell 2000 is up 19.5% YTD vs S&P 500 +10.4%, hitting its 20th all-time high of 2026. QQQ call vol is at a 7-year extreme vs SPY; 22V recommends SPY/IWM calls over expensive QQQ calls. AI trade characterized as mid-cycle slowdown, not bubble unwind, with materials/chemicals emerging as next AI supply-chain beneficiaries.

bullets.title: 10-Year Yields Range-Bound 4.4–4.5%; Fiscal Deficit Supporting Demand Without Bubble Dynamics
bullets.body: Fed Financial Accounts show household and corporate sectors with healthy balance sheets; the large fiscal deficit is sustaining aggregate demand at full employment without bubble dynamics. Market-based r* has recently pushed above g*, making fiscal sustainability more relevant, and nonfinancial debt growth is quickening in typical late-cycle fashion. 22V expects 10-year yields to remain in the 4.4–4.5% range pending clarity on the growth slowdown.

bullets.title: AI Inference Dominance: NVDA Share Rises to 74%; OpenAI Below 50% Market Share for First Time
bullets.body: NVDA's inference chip market share rose to 74% from 66% over the past year; inference is expected to reach two-thirds of AI workloads by end-2026 vs. one-third in 2023. NVDA's Blackwell NVL72 scored highest on the first Agentic AI benchmark, running 20x more agents/MW than HGX H200. Separately, OpenAI's ChatGPT fell below 50% market share for the first time — Gemini at 27.7%, Claude at 10.3% — while OpenAI burned $34B in 2025 ($19B R&D, $6B S&M) against $13B revenue.

bullets.title: China AI Price War: Per-Token Costs Down ~80% Y/Y; Broader Adoption Bullish for Downstream
bullets.body: ByteDance, Tencent, Xiaomi, MiniMax, Alibaba, and DeepSeek have cut LLM model/API pricing 50–99%, driving per-1M-token costs down ~80% y/y in China via architecture improvements and inference optimization. 22V and MS both note that lower token prices support broader AI adoption despite commoditization concerns, and that AI buildout baskets (memory, compute, power, cooling) stabilized after initial declines. Chinese ADRs were under premarket pressure on these LLM price competition reports.

bullets.title: HDD Momentum Surge: WDC +16%, STX +9% on Bullish Asia Checks; FY28 EPS 70% Above Consensus
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley published a bullish HDD sector update citing Asia supply chain checks showing vendors targeting $25–30/TB pricing over 2–3 years vs. current <$15/TB. WDC and STX were both up ~270–280% YTD before yesterday's additional move. Mizuho separately confirmed CPO and 800V DC power transition schedules remain on track for volume production in 2028–2029.

bullets.title: FOXA Acquires ROKU for $160/Share ($22B EV); Deal Shifts Fox Toward 50% Streaming by FY30
bullets.body: Fox Corp is acquiring Roku for $160/share (60% cash / 40% stock) at a $22B EV. Pro-forma entity targets $23B revenue and $5B EBITDA by FY27E (~7% EBITDA CAGR), with $9–10 FCF/share by FY30 and linear TV exposure falling to ~50% by FY30. Citi sees $400M in synergies worth 7x EV/EBITDA; Benchmark flags the deal as positive for TTD, which provides open programmatic demand essential for FOXA to monetize combined inventory. Wedbush pre-emptively downgraded ROKU to neutral.

bullets.title: Mag7 Productivity Advantage: 3x Sales/Employee vs. S&P 500; AI Services Outperforming AI Usage Names
bullets.body: 22V quant analysis shows Mag7 median real sales per employee at ~$2.2M, roughly 3x other S&P 500 constituents, with inflation-adjusted S&P 1500 sales/employee at a record high. AI Services companies (those enabling AI) show better efficiency growth than AI Usage names, explaining their relative outperformance since early 2025. The top quintile sales-per-employee basket is up 17.8% YTD.

bullets.title: NVDA Plans $25B Debt Raise; AVGO Using $35B Apollo/Blackstone Vehicle for Custom XPU Financing
bullets.body: NVDA is planning to raise $25B in new corporate debt — its first bond sale since raising $5B in 2021. Separately, AVGO is using a $35B financing vehicle with Apollo and Blackstone to fund custom XPU buildout for Google, Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI.

bullets.title: Momentum Rotation Underway in Semis: NVDA 'Thrown Out' Despite Cheap Valuation; Next Baskets Emerging
bullets.body: Mizuho notes momentum investors rapidly rotated from optical stocks (Jan–Apr winners) into memory and CPU subsectors, with NVDA described as 'thrown out' of momentum despite strong fundamentals. AVGO fell 22% post-earnings as momentum money rotated on TPU share loss fears at Google. Potential next momentum baskets cited: SMID-cap semi equipment, 800V DC power, satellite/space, and physical AI/robotics.

bullets.title: Germany ZEW Jumps 20.7pts to 10.2 on Oil Price Normalization; Eurozone Growth Still Only 1.0%
bullets.body: Germany's ZEW investor expectations surged 20.7 points to 10.2 in June as oil prices faded and uncertainty eased, while Eurozone Current Conditions slid to a YTD low. PMI models point to sluggish 1.0% growth for Germany and the Eurozone this year versus 3.0% for the US, with ECB having hiked into slowing activity and markets pricing at least one more hike. Eurozone STOXX hit a record high but is still underperforming the S&P on fundamentals.

bullets.title: Hormuz Closure Didn't Trigger Recession; European Rotation Question Re-opens
bullets.body: UBS strategist notes 3.5 months of Strait of Hormuz closure could have pushed the world economy into recession but did not, raising questions about whether rotation from US to European equities can resume. Middle East de-escalation optimism has already boosted equities broadly while pressuring crude oil per the Goldman hedge fund wrap.

bullets.title: May Hedge Fund Performance: Global HFs +2.0%; TMT/Semi Specialists Led; Macro/CTA Muted
bullets.body: Goldman's May HF wrap shows global hedge funds up +2.0% on a strategy-weighted basis, with fundamental equity L/S leading for a second consecutive month. TMT specialists outperformed driven by the semiconductor rally; Asia-focused managers benefited from China tech and Japan. Systematic macro/CTA was muted in May despite strong YTD results. S&P 500 logged its ninth consecutive weekly gain.

bullets.title: Nuclear/Uranium Structural Upcycle: China Targeting 150GW by 2035; AI Power Demand Adding Tailwind
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley initiates Kazatomprom at Overweight ($83 PT) citing a structural uranium upcycle from years of underinvestment. China is targeting 150GW of nuclear capacity by 2035 vs. ~60GW today; the US is targeting a 4x increase by 2050. AI data center power demand is an incremental catalyst for nuclear adoption on top of decarbonization and energy security drivers.

bullets.title: Consumer Resilient but Value-Conscious; Redbook Sales +9.4%, Unit Volumes Declining
bullets.body: Circana May data shows consumer spending +1.3% while unit sales fell 1.5%, with private label now ~50% of apparel sales and discretionary unit volumes down 4.3% implying ~5.7% price increases. Redbook retail sales accelerated to +9.4% (+30bps sequentially). Goldman May credit data shows card delinquencies stable-to-lower y/y, with net charge-offs poised to outperform in Q2 — consistent with a resilient but trade-down consumer backdrop.

bullets.title: AI-Driven Margin Sentiment Elevated; Early Quantifiers Guide ~85bps Improvement from AI Tools
bullets.body: 22V notes companies deploying AI show higher margin sentiment than non-users across sectors; early quantifiers in Q1 guided to ~85bps of margin improvement from AI tools. Key risk flagged: recent productivity gains may partly reflect capital/labor utilization surge and immigration slowdown rather than AI-specific gains. Companies with higher sales/employee show strongest Quality and Size factor exposures.

bullets.title: AI-Referred Retail Traffic Up 138% Y/Y With 53% Higher Revenue vs. Non-AI Traffic
bullets.body: Per the REIT/retail note, AI-referred retail traffic surged 138% year-over-year in May, with AI-sourced visitors generating 53% higher revenue than non-AI traffic. This supports the broadening of AI monetization beyond hyperscalers into downstream commerce and advertising.
